title: Mirror and Invert a Bit Grid
statement:
You get a grid of bits grid, where every cell is 0 or 1 and all rows have the same length.

Apply two changes to every row: first mirror it (reverse the order of its cells), then invert it (every 0 becomes 1 and every 1 becomes 0).

Return the resulting grid. You may change grid in place and return it.

examples.why: Row 0 mirrored is [0, 1, 1], inverted [1, 0, 0]. Row 1 is its own mirror and only inverts. Row 2 mirrors to [0, 0, 1] and inverts to [1, 1, 0].
Inverting alone would give [0, 1] for the first row. The mirror step matters.
A row that reads the same both ways only gets inverted, including its middle cell.

hints: Do the two steps literally first: reverse each row, then flip each bit. Does the order of the two steps matter?
Mirroring swaps cell i with cell n−1−i. Inverting changes both. Look at what happens to a pair that is equal versus a pair that differs.
Walk two pointers inward from both ends of a row. If the two bits are equal, flip both. If they differ, mirroring and inverting cancel out, so leave them. The middle cell of an odd row always flips.

explain.intuition:
The direct way is fine: reverse the row, then XOR every bit with 1. Both steps are O(cols) per row.

You can also do both in one pass. Mirroring swaps cells i and j = n−1−i, and then both get inverted. If the two bits were different, say 1 and 0, swapping gives 0 and 1, and inverting gives back 1 and 0: nothing changes. If they were equal, the swap does nothing and both just flip. So only equal pairs, and the middle cell, need work.
steps: For each row, set i = 0 and j = cols − 1.
While i < j: if row[i] === row[j], flip both. Move i right and j left.
If i === j after the loop (odd length), flip that middle cell.
pitfalls: Forgetting the middle cell of an odd-length row. It is its own mirror, but it still gets inverted.
Using ~x to invert. In JavaScript ~1 is -2, not 0. Use x ^ 1 or 1 - x.
Mirroring the whole grid top to bottom instead of each row left to right.

solutions.title: Reverse, then invert
solutions.idea: Do exactly what the statement says on every row.

solutions.title: One pass with two pointers
solutions.idea: Equal pairs flip, unequal pairs stay, the middle cell flips.
